target.source_quote: ERCOT has issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) seeking one or more Must-Run Alternatives (MRA) to a Reliability Must-Run (RMR) contract with CPS Energy to address projected reliability needs associated with the proposed suspension of BRAUNIG\_VHB1, BRAUNIG\_VHB2, and BRAUNIG\_VHB3 (“Braunig Resources”).  ERCOT has also posted, on the MIS Secure Area, the Parts III of the Notifications of Suspension of Operations (NSO) for the Braunig Resources, which CPS Energy submitted today.
target.target_description: Earliest documented issued solicitation recovered for the Braunig retirement response. Original RFP version 1.0, notice M-C031324-05, July 9 prospective docket schedule and December 3 board paper agree on July 25, 2024. Broader seasonal MRA reliability-service competition via QSEs, not a direct mobile-generator rental order. No earlier issued solicitation was found in this scoped search.

lead_time.note: No numerical advantage is claimed: the earliest recovered March notice and July solicitation lack acceptable independent availability proof. April 23 and July 9 docket receipts establish dated precursors but do not repair the target timestamp. Remove the previous indicative 233-day December-based result. Later confirmation dates must not replace first issuance to inflate warning. July 9 procurement scheduling is already discoverable conventionally, so RFP-release lead time alone would not establish a unique detector advantage.

blockers: Independent accepted availability proof for March 13 notice and July 25 first solicitation remains missing; LISTSERV date corroboration is preserved but is not a press-wire, exchange/regulator release or docket receipt. No schema proof rules were weakened.
Original RFP is broad MRA reliability-service procurement via QSEs. BRIDGE_OR_INTERIM is a qualified service-duration mapping, not temporary/rental equipment evidence; human scope review required.

No identified potential equipment-rental customer or eligible winning QSE in the first RFP; no qualified MRA proposals were received according to the December board material. Vendor eligibility, location/effectiveness and operating constraints must be evaluated before inferring a supplier opportunity.
No named human has reviewed this dossier; it has not entered the accepted cohort. This is a historical case, not an active sales lead.

Earliest means earliest documented issued solicitation recovered in the notices, original RFP, PUCT filings and board materials searched; not an exhaustive proof that no earlier private discussion or public planning signal existed.
reviewer_checklist: Check original July 25 RFP version 1.0 and notice against stored captures; December board paper explicitly calls July 25 the original RFP.

Re-prove public availability using an accepted independent source before assigning lead_time.days. Do not treat the July 9 planned release date or August 9 retrospective filing as proof of exact July 25 publication.
Decide whether broad interim reliability-service procurement belongs in the intended cohort; do not count it as demonstrated rental demand.
Check QSE-only contractual route, geographical effectiveness and technical eligibility; distinguish ERCOT buyer from PUCT regulator, CPS utility, CenterPoint lessee and Life Cycle contractor.
Compare against advance procurement scheduling as well as formal RFP discovery; name a human reviewer only after that person actually completes review.
target_fit_note: Closest existing schema category for seasonal reliability service during April 2025-March 2027. The RFP admits generation, storage and demand response and contracts only with qualified QSEs. This label describes the bounded service period, NOT proof of temporary equipment procurement, a rental requirement, or a rental customer. Keep out of a rental-positive cohort pending explicit scope review.
later_procurement_events: 2024-08-09: PUCT 55999 item 53 filing receipt at 14:56:29 CDT corroborates July 25 RFP issuance; capture braunig-20261023-puct-august9. This is retrospective corroboration, not a replacement procurement date. Cover-letter printed July 18, 2023 conflicts with receipt/context; use receipt only for availability.

2024-08-21: Revised MRA RFP; eventual proposal deadline October 7, 2024, per December board paper (capture braunig-20261023-december-board). Original July RFP deadline was September 9. Original KSAT August signal s2 is later than the first solicitation and was removed from signals; its capture remains unchanged.

2024-12-03: Board staff paper describes original July 25 RFP, August revision and no qualified proposals; recommends Unit 3 RMR and further evaluation of mobile generation for Units 1-2. Capture braunig-20261023-december-board is a staff recommendation, not itself board minutes proving the vote.

2024-12-20: M-D122024-01 is a SECOND solicitation for alternatives to proposed use of CenterPoint-leased Life Cycle generators and Braunig Units 1-2. Original capture ercotmobile2025-notice remains unchanged; printed-date-only, not earliest procurement.

2025-02-25 (KSAT/Texas Tribune article printed 'Published: February 25, 2025 at 2:37 PM'; earliest Wayback CDX snapshot 20250225210210, an upper bound; capture ercotmobile2025-ksat-approval): ERCOT board approval of the Life Cycle mobile-generation plan. Exact text: 'Texas’ main grid operator on Tuesday approved a $54 million plan to replace two aging natural gas-powered plants near San Antonio with the massive mobile generators that CenterPoint Energy came under fire for not deploying in the wake of Hurricane Beryl in July.' and '15 mobile generators currently leased by CenterPoint will be moved from Houston to San Antonio this summer.'

2025-06-04: Effective date printed on Agreement for Emergency Generation Service between ERCOT and Prime Power Solutions LLC d/b/a Life Cycle Power (capture braunig-20261023-emergency-agreement). Recitals identify Life Cycle as mobile-generator owner/operator, CenterPoint as existing lessee under 2021 lease, and release of lease obligations enabling ERCOT service. This is a later emergency-generation service agreement, not an award under the original July competition; printed effective date is not independent publication proof.
